subject: Streaming warmup and dry-run orchestration for Oct test window
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@glintdata.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming warmup and dry-run orchestration for Oct test window

Thanks for the call today — quick recap from our side and some asks so we can run the dry-run next week. High level: we want to validate streaming behavior for short chat sessions (avg 3 turns), confirm 95th latency for chunked streaming under sustained concurrency, and run a throughput sweep to estimate token/sec cost.

What we can provide immediately: k6 scripts (attached), a list of test runner IPs (we can add to an allowlist), and a small sample dataset to exercise streaming chunks. Questions from our engineers:
- What is the best way to provide an API key scoped to a dry-run zero-cost account?
- Can we get a dedicated model slot or an isolated routing policy during the 2-hour window?
- Any special headers we should include for streaming chunk sizes?

Attached: glint-k6-scripts-v1.tar.gz, customer-ip-list.csv

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the scripts.

--
Sarah Lin
SRE Lead, GlintData
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@glintdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming warmup and dry-run orchestration for Oct test window

Sarah — thanks for the prompt deliverables and the scripts. Quick answers inline, then proposed next steps.

Answers:
- Dry-run API key: We can mint a scoped key that only allows the test model and is rate-limited to the window; Ben (cc'd) will provision and upload the key to your shared folder.
- Dedicated slot: We can pin a routing policy to prefer a low-concurrency slot for the 2-hour window (not a full reserved GPU) — that should give predictable p95 behavior. Will confirm exact throughput headroom.
- Streaming headers: No special headers required; our streaming uses chunked HTTP with event-delimited tokens. For your scripts, send prompt and stream=true in body; set Accept: text/event-stream to get chunked frames.

Proposed next steps (we'll track as owners):
1) Ben to create scoped API key (owner: Ben) — ETA 10/21 EOD.
2) Customer to add allowlist CIDRs to your customer-ip-list.csv and confirm (owner: Sarah) — ETA 10/20 morning.
3) Priyom + Marissa to run a preflight 30-min warmup on 10/22 to validate tokenization and basic routing.
4) Formal dry-run (2 hrs) scheduled 10/24 16:00-18:00 UTC (tentative) — adjust if needed.

I'll attach a short dryrun-checklist after Ben provisions the key.

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@glintdata.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming warmup and dry-run orchestration for Oct test window

Looping in with the API key and a few provisioning notes. I created a scoped dry-run key (glint-dryrun-2026-10) tied to the test model and constrained to the 2-hour window. I've uploaded the key to the GlintData shared folder and sent a one-time passphrase via separate channel.

Provisioning notes:
- Key restrictions: model=redwood-stream-small-v1, rate_limit=300 req/min, token_limit=30000 total for window.
- Pinning: I requested routing policy pin to low-latency slot; platform will try to keep the same worker pool but it's not a reserved GPU.
- Telemetry: we enabled per-request tracing headers X-RDW-TRACE for the window so we can correlate spans if you share request ids.

Attachments: dryrun-checklist.pdf (contains confirm steps for auth, IPs, and a quick smoke script).

Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@glintdata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor Hayes <connor.h@glintdata.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming warmup and dry-run orchestration for Oct test window

Thanks Ben — we found the key and the checklist. Quick status update from our side:
- IPs added and confirmed (customer-ip-list.csv).
- We ran the preflight today for 30 minutes as discussed — saw a small increase in head-of-line latency when concurrency hit ~120 streams, p95 climbed to ~420ms for chunk arrival (our previous expectation was ~300ms). We captured traces and have a small set of request ids in the shared drive (link above).

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood run a concurrent probe from your side during the main dry-run to compare internal routing differences? That would help isolate whether the extra latency is client-side (script behavior) or server-side.
2) If p95 > 350ms during the 2-hour run, will Redwood accept this as a failed objective that triggers an immediate rollback to the alternate model variant? We'd like a clear gating policy.

Happy to push the main dry-run to 10/25 if that gives you more time to instrument.

--
Sarah
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@glintdata.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-25T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming warmup and dry-run orchestration for Oct test window

Sarah — thanks for the preflight results and for surfacing the p95 delta. Proposed resolution and clear next steps: 

1) Redwood concurrent probe: Neha will run a parallel probe during the main dry-run to generate identical traffic profiles from our infra (owner: Neha). This will give us a side-by-side baseline and remove variability from your runners.
2) Gating policy: agreed — if p95 chunk latency for sustained concurrency exceeds 350ms for more than 5 consecutive minutes in the 2-hour window, we will automatically switch routing to the alternate model variant (redwood-stream-stable-v1) and mark the dry-run as failed for the original slot. We will capture traces and provide a postmortem within 48 hours.
3) New schedule: main dry-run moved to 2026-10-27 15:00-17:00 UTC to allow for extra instrumentation. Please confirm by EOD 10/26.

Action owners summary:
- Sarah: confirm new window and reconfirm test IPs (ETA 10/26 noon).
- Ben: confirm telemetry payloads and ensure X-RDW-TRACE correlation (ETA 10/26 EOD).
- Neha: run side-by-side probe during window (ETA on-run).
- Priyom/Marissa: run stakeholder notification and follow up on contract gating language if needed.

If that all looks good I will update HubSpot and schedule a brief 15-min incident playbook walk-through prior to the run.

Thanks — Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
